newsitem.title: USA: Clinton-Yeltsin summit delayed one day.
newsitem.headline: Clinton-Yeltsin summit delayed one day.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's summit meeting this week with Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki will be delayed by one day because of Clinton's knee surgery, the White House said on Sunday.

"In order to provide the president with an additional day to recuperate, President Clinton and President Yeltsin have agreed to delay the start of the summit in Helsinki by one day," White House spokesman David Johnson said.
Clinton will leave Washington late on March 19 and arrive in Helsinki midday Thursday.

The White House on Saturday had said there had been no discussion of delaying or significantly altering Clinton's plans for the two-day summit with Yeltsin, whose own health has been more of a concern than that of Clinton's.

Clinton tore his tendon in a freak accident on Friday when he lost his footing on a step at the Florida home of Australian golf professional Greg Norman. He was operated on Friday at Bethesda National Navy Medical Centre.
Johnson said that the previously announced summit schedule would remain essentially the same.
Clinton's planned visit to Denmark will be postponed until July, Johnson said.
He said the president expressed appreciation to the governments of Denmark, Finland and Russia for agreeing to the postponement.
Clinton experienced some sharp pain on Saturday after an emergency surgery to repair a torn tendon on his right knee.
He is due to be discharged from the hospital in suburban Maryland on Sunday.
